newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Survey shows Peters poor choice for NZ Treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows Peters poor choice for NZ Treasurer.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters has his work cut out convincing business he will be a good Treasurer, according to an Evening Post/Business Research Centre poll released on Monday.
Only 14 percent of Wellington region firms surveyed said Peters was the right choice as Treasurer, compared to nearly half signalling the nation's top finance job should have gone to someone else.
One in three firms said Peters was a poor choice, while 16 percent said he was a very poor choice. A further 16 percent were indifferent and 21 percent said they did not know.
The poll, commissioned by The Evening Post and performed by the Business Research Centre, covered 300 big and small businesses in Wellington, Porirua, Kapiti and Hutt Valley.
It was carried out in the days following Peters' attendance at the Government to Business forum on February 11, at which he made his first major speech to industry leaders as Treasurer.
In his speech Peters attempted to soothe concerns he would be irresponsible or unsettling to the business community. He said he would not intervene in financial markets for short-term gain.
The widening of the Reserve Bank's inflation target, to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent, won strong endorsement in the poll.
Sixty percent of firms either agreed or agreed strongly with the wider target, while 19 percent disagreed. A further 21 percent were indifferent or did not know.
Survey results on the value of the dollar failed to give unequivocal backing to business lobby group claims that the currency is too high.
While 35 percent of firms said the dollar was over-valued, 54 percent said the dollar was about right. Five percent said the currency was too low and six percent did not know.
